title: Trivial path is reached by every input
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice inputs in $X$ and Bob inputs in $Y$, and let $\pi$ be a subprotocol path witnessing that a subprotocol $s$ is a rooted subtree of $p$. If deleting the path $\pi$ from $p$ returns no protocol — which occurs precisely when the path is trivial, so that $s = p$ — then every input pair $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ reaches $s$ along $\pi$, meaning $x$ is consistent with all of Alice's choices along $\pi$ and $y$ is consistent with all of Bob's choices along $\pi$.
hypotheses_covered: a subprotocol path from s to p
replaced:
If $\texttt{deletePath}\;\texttt{hsp} = \texttt{none}$ (meaning $s = p$), then every input pair
$(x, y)$ satisfies $\texttt{reachesPath}\;\texttt{hsp}\;x\;y$.
